paras: The killing of Charley Tolbert took place on a county road near Rosanky, Texas, on the afternoon of August 16, 1900, when two white men on horseback beat and shot dead Tolbert, a Black man driving a wagon with his wife and child. According to the accounts, the attack followed Tolbert's refusal to give the road to the riders, and the attackers were never identified. Texas papers called it murder 'without provocation,' and the report reached the governor's Executive Office at Austin, where trouble among local Black residents was feared.

Tolbert was driving toward town with his wife and a small child when two white men on horseback met the wagon and demanded the road. The Austin report said the riders wanted it because the side road was very muddy, while the Freie Presse für Texas wrote that Tolbert refused to turn out of the middle of the road because it was so muddy. When he declined, the two began beating him over the head, with quirts in the Houston Post's account and with heavy switches in the German paper's.

Tolbert's wife begged the men to spare her husband's life. The Austin report and the Houston correspondent said both men then drew their guns and shot him dead, while the Freie Presse said one of them shot him through the chest. He fell into his wife's lap, the riders rode away, and she drove on into Rosanky and reported the killing.

Squire Moore held an inquest, at which the widow said she had never seen the two men before and could not recognize them if they were caught. The Houston Post's correspondent wrote that efforts were being made to bring the guilty parties to justice, but the Austin special described the men as 'unknown.' No report of an arrest, grand jury action or trial appears in the coverage.

The story ran first in Texas papers on August 17, when the San Antonio Daily Light gave it one line in its telegraph column: 'Two white men murder a negro at Rosanky, Texas, without provocation.' The same day the Houston Post printed a longer local account that said the men 'were bent on murder' and gave no motive except that they wanted to warn 'other negroes to give the road to white people.' San Antonio's German-language Freie Presse für Texas called it 'a hideous act of violence' ('Ein scheußlicher Gewaltakt') and the attackers brutes.

Outside Texas, the St. Louis Republic ran an Austin special on August 18 under the headline 'NEGRO MAN KILLED. Refused to Give the Road to White Texans,' which put Tolbert's refusal first and closed on the official fear of trouble among Black residents. In the Black press the killing appeared two weeks later, on August 31, as a single line in the Topeka Colored Citizen's 'Race News' column, which named 'Charlie Tolbert, a colored man' but said nothing of the road dispute or the attackers. No editorial comment on the killing was found in either press.

bases: Two white men on horseback beat and shot dead a Black man on a county road near Rosanky after he refused to give them the road; the papers describe two attackers, not a mob or crowd, and no accusation of crime (A2, A3, A4).

An Austin special based on a report to the Executive Office (A4), a Houston Post correspondent's account with inquest details (A2), and the Freie Presse item (A3) agree on the victim, the two white riders, the road dispute and the shooting, and the Black weekly Colored Citizen confirms the name and killing (A5).

accounts.label: Report to the Executive Office (Austin special)
accounts.gist: Two white men on horseback met the Tolberts on the county road and demanded the road because the side road was muddy; when Tolbert declined they beat him over the head and, as his wife begged for mercy, both drew revolvers and shot him dead.

accounts.label: Houston Post correspondent
accounts.gist: The men beat Tolbert with quirts, ignored his wife's pleas and shot him so that he fell into her lap; the only motive given was a wish to warn Black people to give the road to whites; an inquest was held and the widow could not identify the men.

accounts.label: Freie Presse für Texas
accounts.gist: The riders demanded the middle of the road; Tolbert refused to turn out because the road was very muddy; they struck him with heavy switches and one of them shot him through the chest.

accounts.label: Colored Citizen brief
accounts.gist: Charlie Tolbert, a colored man, was shot and killed near Rosankey while driving along the road in his wagon.

framing.detail: The San Antonio Daily Light's telegraph column said two white men 'murder a negro' at Rosanky 'without provocation.'
The Houston Post account said the men 'were bent on murder' and gave no motive but warning Black people to yield the road.
The Freie Presse called it 'Ein scheußlicher Gewaltakt' (a hideous act of violence) and the attackers 'rohen Menschen' (brutes).
The St. Louis Republic headlined 'Refused to Give the Road to White Texans' and stressed the fear of trouble among Black residents.
The Colored Citizen ran a single unheadlined line in its 'Race News' column, without comment or mention of the road dispute.
